newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Hotel Melia sale hoped for March.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Hotel Melia sale hoped for March.

text.p: The fifth attempted auction of Venezuela's unfinished luxury hotel and shopping complex, Hotel Melia, will probably take place in March, said sources at Venezuela's Banco Industrial (BIV).

"We're just setting a new base price, which shouldn't vary much from the old price of 15.41 billion bolivars ($32.4 million)," the source said. Once that price is set, "we hope to have the new auction in March," he added.

An attempted sale in December was called off after bidders failed to post sufficient guarantees. Then, U.S. company Entertainment Resorts Development International and Switzerland's C.S.L. Credito Subalpino Di Lugano had shown interest in buying the complex.
The source said three new groups had so far voiced interest -- an Irish, a Mexican and a French.
Construction of the hotel complex in Caracas started in 1987 but ground to a halt in 1994 when the then-owner could no longer meet bank payments and the property was transferred to the BIV.
